# Theme 4 Review

<!-- This file is the source of a page on the course website. Read it there: https://ai.buas.nl/open-courses/introduction-to-ml/self-study/theme-4/02_review.html -->

You have learned to combine preprocessing and a model into one object. This page sums up the theme and checks the main ideas.

## Summary

- [Pipelines & ColumnTransformer](01_pipelines_and_columntransformer.ipynb):
  - A `Pipeline` chains transformers and a model: one `fit`, one `predict`, and you save one object.
  - In cross-validation, a pipeline fits every step in each fold on the training part only, so no information from the validation folds leaks into the preprocessing.
  - A `ColumnTransformer` gives different columns different preprocessing; `make_column_selector`, `OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown="ignore")` and `get_feature_names_out` help with real data.
  - Parameters of a step are set as `step__parameter`, which lets you tune the preprocessing and the model together.

## Quiz

These questions are easy if you have worked through the activities. Choose an answer to see whether it is right and why.

::: {.quiz data-answer="2"}
Why does a pipeline make cross-validation correct?

- It makes the training faster, so you can use more folds in the same time. [Speed is not the point. The point is what each step learns from.]{.feedback}
- It refits the preprocessing in each fold, on the training part. [Right. The validation folds then play no part in the preprocessing.]{.feedback}
- It chooses the best model for you by trying them all. [A pipeline does not choose a model; you still compare models yourself.]{.feedback}
:::

::: {.quiz data-answer="1"}
A pipeline has an `SVR` step called `model`. How do you set its `C` to 10?

- `pipeline.set_params(model__C=10)` [Right: the step name, two underscores, then the parameter name.]{.feedback}
- `pipeline.set_params(C=10)` [The pipeline would not know which step `C` belongs to.]{.feedback}
- `pipeline.steps[1].C = 10`, the second step of the pipeline [`steps[1]` is the pair (name, step), not the SVR itself. Use the step name and two underscores.]{.feedback}
:::

::: {.quiz data-answer="3"}
Your data has numeric columns and one column with text categories. Which tool gives each type of column its own preprocessing?

- A `StandardScaler`, which scales every column. [A scaler cannot handle text, and it treats all columns the same way.]{.feedback}
- A second model for the text column. [You need one model; the preprocessing differs per column.]{.feedback}
- A `ColumnTransformer`. [Right, for example with a scaler for the numeric columns and a `OneHotEncoder` for the categories.]{.feedback}
:::
